fr.elements: Main Building; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Road; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing; Detached Structure; Street Frontage; Open Terrain
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Limited Rear Access; Open Terrain; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the single access point and extended driveway remain clear of parked vehicles and movable obstructions could significantly improve apparatus ingress and egress, particularly given the limited rear access around the structure. Marking or identifying the access point from the street frontage may assist responding units in locating the entry quickly during low-visibility conditions. Coordinating with local emergency services to pre-familiarize personnel with the single-entry configuration and the relationship between the main building and detached structure could support more effective staging and navigation across the property during an incident.

wildfire.conditions: Continuous Shrub Cover; Scattered Shrubs; Heavy Brush; Brushland Interface; Fuel Continuity; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Long Driveway; Vegetated Access Route; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing fuel continuity within the immediate structure perimeter should be a primary focus, as dense and continuous shrub cover surrounding the residence could limit defensible space and reduce opportunities for suppression operations near the structure. Thinning and separating shrub masses closest to the building, and creating meaningful gaps within the heavier brush concentrations, may reduce the ability of surface fire to travel uninterrupted toward the structure. Managing vegetation along the length of the driveway would support firefighter access and improve evacuation conditions, particularly given the extended travel distance involved. Maintaining cleared margins on both sides of the access route and reducing overhanging or encroaching vegetation could improve visibility and passability during an incident. Preserving and expanding any existing open terrain around the property could serve as a natural fuel break, and continuing to manage vegetation concentrations adjacent to the structure over time would support long-term wildfire resilience and property preparedness.
